To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kidney and the vasculature are the main organs involved in the pathophysiology of chronic kidney disease.

the loss of L-arginine in chronic kidney disease (as in puromycin-induced CKD) results from reduced synthesis and transport, induction of arginasases, and increased endogenous nitric oxide synthase inhibitor asymmetric dimethylarginin (ADMA).

the reduction in L-Arg synthesis in CKD is due to a decrease in ASS/ASL activity and a loss of CAT1 transporters, and that the increase in ADMA is due to a loss of DDAH activity and a loss in renal clearance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of L-Arg and asymmetric dimethylarginines in the pathogenesis of chronic kidney disease.
the role of the L-Arg/NO pathway in the pathogenesis of hypertension in CKD.
the role of arginine in kidney disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kidney damage and hypertension induced in PAN CKD are associated with multiple defects in L-Arg synthesis, uptake and degradation and that oxidative stress may be involved.
reduced renal synthesis, transport, utilization of L-Arg and increased plasma ADMA, all of which will reduce NO production, contribute to renal pathology in PAN-induced CKD.
the reduction in L-Arg and NO bioavailability is multifactorial in this model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PAN-induced kidney disease and hypertension was accompanied by progressive loss of L-Arg synthetic pathways, increased ADMA and oxidative stress.
the loss of L-Arg transporters and enzymes in PAN CKD is a major contributor to NO deficiency.
reduced renal synthesis and uptake of L-Arg and loss of renal and hepatic DDAHD are important in the pathogenesis of CKD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidney is a critical organ for L-Arg synthesis, release and uptake, and the aorta is critical for L-Arg uptake and NO production.
the loss of renal clearance of L-Arg and the loss of DDAH activity are the main factors in the development of hypertension in CKD.
there is an imbalance in L-Arg metabolism in PAN-CKD which is associated with oxidative stress and hypertension.
